Venturing beyond civilization's borders demands more than sharp aim and keen senses; it requires respect for the raw untamed elements. An experienced scout named Lyreena offers guidance to wandering hunters, welcoming them to pause their trek and take comfort by her campfire. In the perilous wilds of Azeroth, knowing how to establish a hearth and replenish one's strength between hunts is just as critical as knowing how to track quarry.

A roaring campfire provides comfort against the nocturnal cold, offering a moment of calm where weary travellers can shake off fatigue. Sitting close to the blaze allows adventurers to gain Boosted Rest, revitalizing their energy and preparing them for the rigors of exploration. Taking time to sit by the embers teaches young adventurers that patience and rest are enduring pillars of wilderness survival.
Lyreena is an experienced wilderness mentor who teaches aspiring adventurers and hunters how to properly rest and survive out in the elements. She offers practical advice around her campfire.

The Great Outdoors is an introductory survival lesson offered by seasoned travelers to newly minted wanderers across Azeroth. By taking a moment to rest by a warm campfire, fledglings learn how staying well-rested and prepared keeps an adventurer alive beyond city walls. It marks the first step into mastering wilderness survival and specialized field camps.

No matter how sharp your blade or potent your magic, the wilds of Azeroth quickly whittle down anyone who neglects the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers stationed near roadside clearings offer this simple lesson to travelers setting out from their home valleys. Taking time to rest by a campfire does more than ease sore boots—it settles the mind and readies the spirit for the harsh road ahead. Only those who master the discipline of regular rest and preparation stand a chance of surviving long enough to claim fortune and glory.

Once an adventurer grasps the value of a crackling fire and proper rest, the instructors point them directly toward town tradesfolk. A camp in the field is rarely complete with just an ember and a bedroll; survival requires practical crafts. Whether forging replacement rivets, cooking trail rations, or stitching torn gear under the stars, every profession provides unique camp fixtures to turn a barren hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

Cutting Teeth is the initial trial given to fresh recruits arriving in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Overseer Gornek assigns newcomers to thin the mottled boar population roaming the nearby cactus dirt farms, testing their basic combat readiness. Surviving this modest rite of passage proves an aspiring warrior or spellcaster possesses the backbone necessary to serve the Horde.

The Valley of Trials does not indulge delusions of grandeur. While young recruits might dream of pursuing massive beasts across the Barrens or winning glory on battlefields, overseer Gornek begins their evaluation with far more grounded matters. Thinning the mottled boars around the valley farms serves as a baseline assessment: it ensures a recruit knows how to wield a weapon or cast a spell, can handle wild aggression, and possesses enough sense to survive their very first skirmish.

Beyond testing raw recruits, culling the mottled boars serves a practical domestic purpose for the red desert settlement. The feral swine roam the dirt farms north and northeast of the camp, rooting through cactus patches and threatening the scarce supplies cultivated in Durotar's harsh soil.
